name: OPA partial evaluation -> JPA Specification (row-level filtering)
description: For list endpoints, instead of fetching all rows then filtering in-memory, send the ABAC query to OPA's compile API (partial evaluation) to get back residual conditions, then translate those conditions into a JPA Criteria Specification (or QueryDSL predicate) applied at the database. This pushes authorization into the SQL WHERE clause — correct and efficient. This is the library's differentiating feature; the one comparable OSS project (opa-data-filter) is unmaintained.

name: Batch action evaluation for list endpoints
description: When checking many resources' actions at once (e.g. which actions a user may take on each item in a page), batch them into a single OPA evaluation with adaptive chunking rather than one call per item. Large measured speedups for list endpoints versus per-item calls. Keep a sane chunk size and make it configurable.

OPA response-wrapper DTOs that omit @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) break deserialization the moment OPA decision logging is enabled, because every response then carries an extra 'decision_id' field. The client throws 'Unrecognized field decision_id' and (if it falls back to deny-all) silently denies everything.
resolution: Put @JsonIgnoreProperties(ignoreUnknown=true) on EVERY OPA response wrapper class (and nested decision classes), not just some. Add a test that deserializes a response containing an unknown field.

name: Distinguish error-DENY_ALL from policy-DENY_ALL in partial-eval residuals
description: A failed Compile call (transport/non-200/unparseable) and a policy-unsatisfiable answer both collapse to DENY_ALL, but they must compose differently: a POLICY deny may legitimately be OR-widened (e.g. a hierarchy subtreeSpec alongside an unsatisfiable tag branch), while an ERROR deny means there is no policy answer at all — nothing may widen, no batch fallback may run, the whole list fails closed. Implemented as PartialResult.fromError + PartialResult.error(); AbacQueryService returns List.of() before any composition when fromError. General rule: any Java-side predicate that mirrors a policy clause (SubtreeSpecResolver mirrors inherited_grant) must never outlive the policy engine it mirrors — gate it on 'we actually heard from OPA'.

After Phase 5.97 moved id'd decisions to the gate (role resolved on the GOVERNING ROOT; role-def ABSENT at the root -> the realm fallback decides, the pinned E4 semantic), the hierarchy matrix's re-parent flip cell -- written in 5.5-A when layer-3 HierarchicalAuthorizer denied role-less reads outright -- started legitimately answering 200 for a realm-viewer on a team-less foreign root. The 403 it asserted had been produced by a deny MECHANISM the slice replaced, not by the semantics it claimed to pin. A stale mechanism hides behind a green assert until the rig is rebuilt.
resolution: Make the negative cell role-DRIVEN: bind the reader to a deliberate no-grant role (permissions {}) on a team governing the foreign root, so role-def-present disables the fallback (the E3 semantic) and the flip stays provable for the right reason (run-hierarchy-matrix.sh, fixed on the audit-followups-hardening branch). Rule for future slices that change WHO/WHERE a deny comes from: sweep every negative e2e cell and ask 'which mechanism produces this 4xx today?'

name: Cross-table ltree subtree re-parent + GiST index + recursive-CTE backfill (multi-table hierarchy adoption)
description: When a resource hierarchy spans MULTIPLE tables (Catalog/Category in one shape, Products in another), an atomic ltree subtree re-parent must rewrite the moved subtree in the PRIMARY table AND its descendant rows in the OTHER table(s) — a single-table UPDATE ... WHERE path <@ oldSelfPath leaves cross-table descendants pointing at the stale lineage. Library method HierarchicalPathMaintainer.reparentDescendantsInTable(table, oldSelfPath, newParent) does the descendant-only rewrite (no new-parent/cycle validation, no min-row requirement — that's the primary reparent() call's job); call both in the same transaction. App-side re-parent ordering that avoids the managed entity overwriting the native rewrite: (1) set parentId on the managed entity + saveAndFlush, (2) entityManager.clear(), (3) native subtree path rewrite, (4) re-read fresh. Liquibase ltree adoption gotchas: ltree's <@ containment operator needs a GiST index (NOT GIN — GIN is for the JSONB tags); backfill nested paths with a recursive CTE; CREATE EXTENSION ltree before the path columns; map the path as a String with @Column(columnDefinition=ltree)+@ColumnTransformer(write='?::ltree'); ddl-auto: validate boots clean as the entity↔migration proof. Read the path via getResultList() not getResultStream() (a lazy stream raises 'ResultSet is closed' after the context is cleared).

repository.deleteAll() on a table with a SELF-referential ON DELETE CASCADE FK (category.parent_id) is an order-dependent optimistic-lock flake in shared-Testcontainers ITs: deleteAll() loads all rows and deletes one-by-one with a version check; deleting a loaded PARENT cascades its children away at the DB level mid-iteration, and deleting the already-cascade-deleted child then hits 0 rows -> ObjectOptimisticLockingFailureException. Only fires when a PRIOR suite left a parent-child tree in the shared container - the suite passes targeted and fails 4/4 in the full run (ProductListIsolationIT, deep-review of the product-tags slice).
resolution: Clean via the ROOT table only (catalogs.deleteAll()) and let the FK cascades clear the children Hibernate never loaded - the CatalogListIsolationIT idiom. Never deleteAll() child tables that self-cascade. Sweep: grep tests for categories.deleteAll()/products.deleteAll() when adding IT seed cleanup.

name: mutate(id, Consumer) as the safe-by-default write path
description: Make the correct-under-concurrency write the easy one: @Transactional MODEL mutate(ID id, Consumer<MODEL> fn) { var e = getByIdForUpdate(id); fn.accept(e); return repo.save(e); } — lock-for-update + apply + save in one tx, so two concurrent mutations of the same row serialize and neither sees a stale @Version. Callers write mutate(id, p -> { p.setX(...); }). Keep slow/external work OUT of fn (the lock is held until commit). Pessimistic mutate is the default; offer an optimistic mutateWithRetry only when blocking is too expensive. Prove serialization with a latch-forced IT on real Postgres (not H2): no StaleObjectStateException escapes, version increments exactly twice, both mutations applied.

The rollback-only trap: catching a @Transactional method's exception INSIDE a TransactionTemplate lambda does NOT produce a clean skip. To skip a write on an expected condition (e.g. the row was deleted), code wrapped getByIdForUpdate(id) in a try/catch(EntityNotFoundException) inside transactionTemplate.executeWithoutResult(...) and returned from the catch. getByIdForUpdate is itself @Transactional(REQUIRED), so it JOINS the template's physical transaction; when it throws, Spring's transaction interceptor marks that shared transaction ROLLBACK-ONLY *before* the catch runs. Swallowing the exception and returning does not clear the mark — so at commit TransactionTemplate.execute throws UnexpectedRollbackException ('Transaction silently rolled back because it has been marked as rollback-only'). The skip therefore fails AFTER logging that it skipped; on an at-least-once trigger (scheduled re-run, message redelivery) it re-fires and fails identically each time. The tell is a contradiction in the logs: the '...skipping' line prints AND the op still errors/retries. INVISIBLE TO UNIT TESTS: a mocked TransactionTemplate runs the lambda synchronously and never models rollback-only commit semantics, so the broken version PASSES its unit test — it only surfaces against a real transaction.
resolution: Pre-check with the UNLOCKED non-throwing finder (findById(id).isEmpty()) BEFORE opening the transaction, and skip there — the exception never crosses a tx boundary. Keep the locked getByIdForUpdate INSIDE the tx as the racing-delete safety net (a row deleted in the window between probe and lock still throws → propagates, the correct outcome for a genuine race — don't pretend it was a clean skip). Alternative: catch OUTSIDE the TransactionTemplate (also correct, but the pre-check reads cleaner and opens no tx for the common skip). With mutate(id, fn) the trap can't arise (no lambda to catch inside — the not-found throw propagates out of mutate). TESTING: prove commit/rollback-dependent fixes with an IT on real Postgres, OR assert the structural invariant a mock CAN see — verify(transactionTemplate, never()).executeWithoutResult(any()) on the skip path pins 'we skipped before the tx'. Added as Rule 7 + 'The rollback-only trap' section in docs/guides/CONCURRENCY-AND-LOCKING.md (clean-room; generalized from a portal-side incident — neutral Product/getByIdForUpdate/EntityNotFoundException domain, no proprietary names). The /deep-review concurrency lens should flag a catch of a @Transactional throw inside a TransactionTemplate lambda.

name: AbacQueryService seam: compile→Specification→query, AND-with-scope, fail-closed allowlist via a fullySupported flag
description: The list-authorization seam tying OPA partial-eval to the DB (layer 3 of the three-layer model). findAuthorized(JpaSpecificationExecutor<T extends AbacDataObject> repo, Specification<T> scope, AbacContext queryContext): (1) opaClient.compile(ctx)->residual; (2) ResidualSpecificationFactory.from(residual)->authzSpec; (3) repo.findAll(scope.and(authzSpec)). TWO LOAD-BEARING INVARIANTS: (a) AND-NEVER-REPLACE — always scope.and(authzSpec), never a bare findAll(authzSpec), so the caller's path scoping (catalogId/categoryId) is preserved and no cross-scope row leaks (prove with an IT: authz=emea AND scope=apac -> empty). (b) NEVER FAIL-OPEN — a partialEval.enabled=false kill-switch degrades to the COARSE pre-Phase-5 path (one opaClient.allow(ctx) check then scope-only), deny->List.of() BEFORE any findAll; the allowlist finisher engages ONLY on !residual.fullySupported() && allowlistFallback. THE fullySupported FLAG (additive core change to PartialResult): a 3rd record component boolean fullySupported (default true via a preserved 2-arg convenience ctor so T1/T3 stay byte-compatible) + a PartialResult.unsupported() factory = a fail-closed DENY_ALL FLAGGED not-fully-SQL. CompileResponseParser returns unsupported() (not plain denyAll()) when it hits an untranslatable term; a clean empty result stays a fully-supported denyAll(). This is how the allowlist escape hatch stays fail-closed: residual not-fully-SQL + allowlist ON -> fetch scoped candidates, build per-row AbacContext (resource=the loaded AbacDataObject's type/id/attributes, same subject/action/roleDef), opaClient.allowAll(perRow), drop false rows (a short/mismatched batch from the client's all-false-on-error also drops rows). allowlist OFF -> just deny (empty). NEVER a blind fetch-all, never a wider set. Bound findAuthorized <T extends AbacDataObject> (the plan said bare <T>) so per-row contexts can be built. Settings carrier: a PartialEvalSettings(enabled, allowlistFallback) record with defaults()=both-on, which the starter binds its partialEval.* properties onto. Test: mock repo + a 3-method stub OpaClient (compile/allow/allowAll programmable) for U20-U24; a Testcontainers IT proving two subjects -> different disjoint row sets + the AND-with-scope no-leak.

name: subtreeOf SPI: fail-closed subtree predicate (ltree ltree_isparent pushdown vs CTE bounded id-IN)
description: The inverse of the ancestor walk for hierarchy-aware LIST filtering (Slice 5.5-B): AncestorResolver.subtreeOf(rootType,rootId) returns a JPA Specification selecting a root's subtree (root-inclusive), to be OR-ed into a list query. TWO impls, strategy behind the SPI. ltree: ltree_isparent(rootPath, entity.path) — the FUNCTION FORM of the @> operator (reverse of <@), so the predicate stays in JPA Criteria (cb.function, no native-SQL operator string); the bound root path is cast via text2ltree(?); the descendant id set is NEVER materialized in Java. CTE: a downward parent_id walk (a new optional DescendantIdSource SPI, childrenOf -> List<ParentRef> carrying types so the walk recurses) materializes the bounded descendant id set -> id IN (...). KEY: unlike ancestorsOf (which THROWS fail-closed), subtreeOf SWALLOWS to an always-false predicate (cb.disjunction()) on any breach/error/missing-source — because it is OR-ed into a query, a no-op widening is the safe collapse, never wider. maxDepth-bounded + cycle-guarded; both impls implement it additively; opa-abac-core untouched.

An ltree subtree re-parent UPDATE 'SET path = newPrefix || subpath(path, oldDepth) WHERE path <@ oldSelfPath' fails with Postgres 'ERROR: invalid positions' on the MOVED NODE's own row, because subpath(path, offset) requires offset < nlevel(path) and for the moved node nlevel(path)==oldDepth (offset==length).
resolution: Guard the moved node's own row with a CASE: 'SET path = CASE WHEN nlevel(path)=oldDepth THEN CAST(newSelfPath AS ltree) ELSE CAST(newSelfPath AS ltree) || subpath(path, oldDepth) END'. The node itself gets just newSelfPath (empty descendant suffix); descendants (nlevel>oldDepth) get the valid subpath. Caught by the Testcontainers re-parent IT.

description: Spring Data JPA auditing (@CreatedDate/@LastModifiedDate) on an OffsetDateTime field throws 'Cannot convert unsupported date type java.time.LocalDateTime to java.time.OffsetDateTime' on save. The default auditing date source emits LocalDateTime and its DateConvertingAuditableBeanWrapper cannot target OffsetDateTime. Hit when the base entities standardized on OffsetDateTime/timestamptz.
resolution: Supply a DateTimeProvider bean returning Optional.of(OffsetDateTime.now()) and reference it via @EnableJpaAuditing(dateTimeProviderRef="..."). Auditing then uses the OffsetDateTime as-is, no conversion. (Same applies to any non-LocalDateTime audit timestamp type.)

name: Residual DNF → JPA Specification over the tags JSONB column (Postgres), SQL/Rego agreement on scalar-vs-array
description: Translate a neutral PartialResult{ALLOW_ALL|DENY_ALL|CONDITIONAL, DNF clauses} into a Spring Data JpaSpecificationExecutor Specification over the tags JSONB column, with NO OPA-wire knowledge in spring-data (clean module boundary: core=Compile API+DNF, spring-data=JSONB→Criteria). Mapping: ALLOW_ALL->Specification.where(null) (no predicate; the caller's path scope still applies AND-ed); DENY_ALL or a null residual->(r,q,cb)->cb.disjunction() (always-false=match-none, the fail-closed shape); CONDITIONAL->cb.or(cb.and(conds)...) over the DNF, with an EMPTY conjunction short-circuiting to cb.conjunction() (always-true). Per-condition via JPA Criteria function() with BOUND literals (no SQL strings, injection-safe, dialect-portable): tags.<k> EQ/NEQ -> cb.equal/notEqual(cb.function('jsonb_extract_path_text',String,root.get('tags'),cb.literal(k)), v); IN -> extractText(...).in(values); CONTAINS (array membership) -> cb.isTrue(cb.function('jsonb_exists',Boolean, cb.function('jsonb_extract_path',Object,tags,literal(k)), literal(v))) i.e. the ? existence operator; an intrinsic (non-tags) path -> root.get('<field>') compare. Centralize the JSONB fn names in a package-private JsonPathDialect seam (Postgres impl) so a 2nd dialect is a seam not a rewrite (don't build a 2nd dialect). CRITICAL SEMANTIC: the Postgres ? operator on a JSONB STRING scalar tests STRING EQUALITY (on an ARRAY it tests element membership) — so 'region CONTAINS emea' matches BOTH a scalar region=='emea' row AND a [emea,amer] array row. This is CORRECT and required: it AGREES with the single-decision Rego whose resource_tag_values normalizes a scalar to a singleton set (mx-666644), so the LIST and a single-GET decide the SAME rows (ADR-0005/0006). Assert it in the IT, don't 'fix' it. TEST POSTURE: a Mockito Criteria-capture unit test (stub cb.function/equal/and/or, verify the calls) PLUS a mandatory Testcontainers IT against REAL Postgres+JSONB (never H2 — jsonb_* and ? are Postgres-only) seeding scalar+array+multi-key rows and asserting EXACT surviving row sets for EQ/IN/CONTAINS/DNF/ALLOW_ALL/DENY_ALL. For the IT in this non-app library module: a nested @SpringBootApplication + @DataJpaTest(replace=NONE) + @Testcontainers, AND @EnableJpaAuditing(dateTimeProviderRef) with a DateTimeProvider returning OffsetDateTime (createdAt is @CreatedDate nullable=false; LocalDateTime provider throws, mx-5fb01d), AND the module's test task needs TESTCONTAINERS_RYUK_DISABLED=true + the resolved podman DOCKER_HOST (copy the example modules' resolveDockerHost()).

name: Per-instance tag-aware load-then-check (when the type-level @OpaPreAuthorize can't see the resource's tags)
description: The pre-invocation @OpaPreAuthorize is TYPE-LEVEL: it evaluates SpEL against method ARGUMENTS before the handler runs, so it cannot supply the resource's attributes (tags) to OPA. For a decision that depends on the resource's tags (a tag-based grant), do an explicit APP-LAYER load-then-check in the controller: load the entity, then call the library's OpaClient directly with the LOADED entity as the AbacContext.Resource (so its tags reach input.resource.attributes) and the role resolved via the governing PARENT (a Category is governed by its Catalog's team, so resolve on (catalog, catalogId), not the category id). This is EXAMPLE-APP code built on the library's public OpaClient + RoleDefinitionSupplier beans — NOT a library change; the general per-instance/hierarchical authorization path belongs in the library at Phase 5. Fail-closed: deny on no-subject / unresolved-role / OPA error. E2E shape that proves it: seed two tag-gated roles (ANY_OF + ALL_OF) and three differently-tagged resources at run time, then assert the decisive same-role/different-tags 200-vs-403 contrast through the gateway. Operational gotcha: tearing the compose rig down/up while the shared network is in use can drop the whole pool — bring base Postgres up first, then the rig, then re-run.

name: Generic pessimistic-lock repository fragment via SpEL #{#entityName}
description: One @NoRepositoryBean fragment serves every entity's 'select for update': @Lock(PESSIMISTIC_WRITE) @Query("SELECT e FROM #{#entityName} e WHERE e.id = :id") Optional<T> findByIdForUpdate(@Param("id") ID id). The SpEL #{#entityName} resolves per concrete repository, so there's no per-entity boilerplate. A concrete repo mixes it in alongside JpaRepository. A generic service guards getByIdForUpdate/mutate with 'instanceof LockableJpaRepository' and throws a clear UnsupportedOperationException if the fragment wasn't mixed in — opt-in and loud, never a silent unlocked read.

name: Opt-in default-off starter wiring for hierarchy: @ConditionalOnBean(source) resolver selection by property
description: Wire N-level hierarchy in the OPA-ABAC starter as a TWO-PART opt-in, default-off. (1) A HierarchyAutoConfiguration nested in OpaAbacAutoConfiguration is gated on @ConditionalOnProperty(opa.abac.hierarchy.enabled=true) WITHOUT matchIfMissing (so absent config ⇒ no beans) AND @ConditionalOnClass(JpaSpecificationExecutor). (2) The AncestorResolver is @ConditionalOnBean on the app-provided data-access SOURCE (LtreePathSource for resolver=ltree default, ParentLinkSource for resolver=cte) — the library can't know the app's table mapping, so it only wires a resolver once the app supplies the matching source; the HierarchicalAuthorizer is @ConditionalOnBean(AncestorResolver). All beans @ConditionalOnMissingBean so an app-supplied resolver/authorizer overrides everything. Properties live in OpaAbacProperties.Hierarchy (enabled/resolver/maxDepth + an inheritable map childType->[ancestorType]); inheritable is surfaced as config but consumed by the REGO (OPA data), not the Java wiring (the starter only uses enabled/resolver/maxDepth to build beans). Regenerate spring-configuration-metadata.json via the configuration-processor. The Phase-5 partial-eval beans/properties stay untouched (hierarchy is purely additive). Verified by ApplicationContextRunner: default-off, ltree/cte selection, no-source→no-resolver, user-override-wins, property binding.

A JPA Criteria 'id IN (...)' predicate built from STRING ids fails against a Postgres uuid column with: ERROR operator does not exist: uuid = character varying. root.get("id").as(String.class).in(stringIds) does NOT cast the column in SQL — it binds varchar literals against the uuid column. Surfaced in the CTE subtreeOf id-IN path (Slice 5.5-B T1) where descendant ids flow through the type-agnostic AncestorResolver SPI as strings.
resolution: Bind the ids as the entity id column's actual type: convert each string id to java.util.UUID when it parses as one (else keep verbatim), so root.get("id").in(uuidList) binds uuid literals. This is the column-type-agreement analogue of the residual's scalar-vs-array care (mx-6876cd). The base entities (BaseModel) all use UUID ids.

name: OPA Compile-API partial-eval → neutral DNF residual (fail-closed at the empty-result boundary)
description: Translate OPA's Compile API (POST /v1/compile, query 'data.<type>.filter == true', unknowns=['input.resource'], resource OMITTED from input) into a Spring-free PartialResult{decision ALLOW_ALL|DENY_ALL|CONDITIONAL, List<Conjunction>} = DNF (OR-of-ANDs), Condition{path, Operator EQ|NEQ|IN|CONTAINS, value}. THE VERIFIED RESULT-SHAPE MAPPING (probed against OPA 1.10.1, and it is the OPPOSITE of what an intuitive reading suggests — getting it wrong is a fail-OPEN whole-table leak): {"result":{}} (empty, no queries key) = query UNSATISFIABLE = DENY_ALL (NOT allow-all!); {"result":{"queries":[[]]}} (a query whose conjunction is EMPTY) = unconditionally true = ALLOW_ALL; {"result":{"queries":[[expr,...]]}} = residual = CONDITIONAL. So ALLOW_ALL must emerge from EXACTLY ONE place — an explicit empty/tautological conjunction — and every other branch (absent result / no queries / unsupported term / any transport-parse error) returns denyAll(). AST per expression: {terms:[opRef, operandA, operandB]}; operator var = eq/equal (EQ), neq (NEQ), internal.member_2 (IN, from 'x in {set}'); 'negated':true folds eq->neq; one operand is a ref into input.resource.* ([{var input},{string resource},{string attributes/<intrinsic>},...]) the other a literal (string/number/boolean/set). Map attributes.<k> -> tags.<k>; an intrinsic (id) stays a column path. CRITICAL: because input.resource is the unknown, the residual ALWAYS includes eq('<type>', input.resource.type) — drop it as a tautology (we scope the SQL to one type), treat any other constraint on type as unsupported->deny. Closed operator set: any unrecognized operator/ref/literal poisons the WHOLE residual -> denyAll() (narrow-but-correct > wide-but-wrong; a mistranslated predicate is a silent data leak). Make compile()+allowAll() ABSTRACT (not default) on OpaClient so a custom client can't inherit a fail-open filter. GOTCHA: a record's static factory method must NOT share a name with one of its boolean component accessors (ExprResult.unsupported() factory clashes with the unsupported() accessor) -> rename to notSupported().

name: AncestorResolver SPI: fail-closed walk owned by the library, data-access via a tiny source SPI, two interchangeable impls
description: N-level hierarchical authorization resolves a leaf's root-first, leaf-excluded ancestor chain (input.resource.ancestors) behind an AncestorResolver SPI. The library owns the correctness-critical WALK (ordering, leaf-exclusion, mandatory cycle detection, mandatory depth bound) and is fail-closed by THROWING AncestorResolutionException — never returning a partial/truncated chain (a truncation could under- or over-grant; callers treat throw as 'no inheritance ⇒ direct grant only', never 'allow'). Per-app DATA ACCESS is a separate one-method source SPI so the resolver stays table-agnostic and unit-testable with in-memory stubs: LtreePathSource(pathOf type,id→Optional<String>) for the default LtreeAncestorResolver (decode a denormalized ltree path in ONE indexed read; throw on missing/NULL/malformed/leaf-mismatch/over-depth) and ParentLinkSource(parentOf type,id→Optional<ParentRef>) for RecursiveCteAncestorResolver (walk live parent_id adjacency hop-by-hop, visited-set cycle detection incl self-loop, depth counter; correct-by-construction on re-parent, no denormalized state). ltree labels allow only [A-Za-z0-9_], so a UUID id is encoded as 32 dash-free hex digits (HierarchyLabels, shared encode/decode so the T3 path-maintainer and the decoder can't drift). Package opa-abac-spring-data.hierarchy imports only core.ParentRef + java.util — zero OPA-wire/residual/Specification coupling; the Phase-5 list filter is untouched (that's Slice 5.5-B). Tested with pure-JUnit (both impls, every fail-closed path) + Testcontainers real Postgres + the ltree extension (never H2).

name: Paged findAuthorized: guard + four paths + PageImpl over the filtered fallback (exact subject-relative count)
description: Paginate an ABAC-filtered list by an ADDITIVE Pageable overload on the query seam (5.95): findAuthorized(repo, scope, ctx, subtreeSpec, Pageable) -> Page<T>. (1) Guard FIRST: pageable.getSort().isUnsorted() -> IllegalArgumentException before any OPA/repo call — pagination without a total order silently repeats/drops rows; services pass a fixed createdAt ASC, id ASC (id tiebreaker = total order). (2) Pure-SQL: the IDENTICAL scope.and(tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec)).and(notDenied) composition paged — extract it to ONE private helper shared by the unpaged and paged paths so they cannot drift. (3) Allowlist fallback: fetch candidates SQL-SORTED with pageable.getSort() (path-independent order vs pure-SQL), batchFilter unchanged (order-preserving), slice the window in memory -> new PageImpl(slice, pageable, survivors.size()) — the survivor count IS the exact count; zero new cost (the path is fetch-all already). (4) Kill-switch: coarse allow then scope.and(notDenied) paged. (5) fromError: Page.empty(pageable), NO repo call — a failed compile empties the page INCLUDING the count (no count leak), and never triggers the fallback. totalElements is the subject-relative authorized total on every path — never items.length. Decisive IT: two subjects 5-vs-3 totals; a perPage=2 walk == the single-page list element-for-element; fallback pages byte-identical to pure-SQL pages.

name: Starter wiring + example adoption for the hierarchy-aware list resolver (SubtreeSpecResolver bean + 4-arg call via ObjectProvider)
description: Wire the 5.5-B list widening as a TWO-PART opt-in mirroring 5.5-A. STARTER: a SubtreeSpecResolver @Bean in HierarchyAutoConfiguration, gated @ConditionalOnBean(AncestorResolver.class) + the existing hierarchy.enabled=true (so it follows the same default-off posture and only wires when an app supplied a data-access source bean), and @ConditionalOnMissingBean (overridable). It reuses the SAME AncestorResolver + RoleDefinitionSupplier as HierarchicalAuthorizer + the inheritance map from properties.getHierarchy().getInheritable() — NO new property. EXAMPLE: the list authorizer injects ObjectProvider<SubtreeSpecResolver> (present only when hierarchy is on) and per-call resolves the subtreeSpec on the SAME governing root the role is resolved on, passing it into the 4-arg findAuthorized; absent provider / no inheritable grant -> null -> the tag-only 3-arg behavior. The always-on AbacQueryService bean injects ObjectProvider<AncestorResolver> for the batch path. SCOPE NOTE recorded: a list endpoint that does NOT already use the Phase-5 AbacQueryService partial-eval path (e.g. a plain repo.findByX scoped query) cannot be widened by subtreeSpec without FIRST adopting the Phase-5 residual filter — so adopting hierarchy on such a list is a larger, separate change, not part of this slice. ddl-auto:validate boot is the proof of no schema change.

name: Deterministic TOCTOU race ITs: two aspect hooks pin the gate-window guard AND the post-guard @Version backstop
description: To prove version-binding 409 contracts deterministically (no sleeps/threads), register a test @Aspect with two get-and-clear AtomicReference<Runnable> hooks: (1) BEFORE_HANDLER on the controller method — an unordered aspect is LOWEST_PRECEDENCE so it runs INSIDE the order-190 method-security interceptor, i.e. after the gate decided+cached and before the handler loads: a JDBC version-bump here must trip the VersionGuard (gate snapshot != fresh load -> 409, mutation not applied); (2) BEFORE_SAVE on the repository save (pointcut: this(XRepository) && execution(* save(..))) — fires after the handler's load+guard, so a bump here forces a stale-@Version merge -> OptimisticLockingFailureException -> the starter's 409 advice (proving the post-guard backstop live, not 500). Together the two hooks cover every gate->write window. Bumps via JdbcTemplate auto-commit so the racing write is visible to the handler's transaction. Gotcha: if the schema's FKs are all ON DELETE CASCADE there is no natural DataIntegrityViolation to test the advice with — the stale-save route is the deterministic alternative.

name: Version binding: gate snapshot guarded against the fresh load via the one JPA @Version -> 409
description: Binding an authorization decision to the state a mutation acts on, without persisting the decision snapshot: reads return the cached authorized snapshot (the response IS the state the decision saw); mutating handlers load fresh in-transaction as always, then VersionGuard.requireUnchanged(snapshot, fresh) BEFORE any write — drift OR a null version throws VersionConflictException (fail loud, one exception type keeps the advice mapping total) -> 409 STATE_CONFLICT problem+json with a STATIC detail; the client re-reads and retries and the retry's gate decides on the new state. The one existing JPA @Version is the version (an ABAC-only counter is a silent-fail-open trap). Layered windows: gate->handler-load is the guard's (deterministic IT via a pre-handler aspect bump); post-guard belongs to @Version + the starter's dao advice (deterministic IT via a pre-save bump). Where a pessimistic lock exists (mutate(id, fn)), guard INSIDE the locked tx against the locked row — decide under the protection you act under.

name: SubtreeSpecResolver: root-only inheritable gate mirroring the Rego inherited_grant for list widening
description: The 'whether to widen' half of the hierarchy-aware list filter (5.5-B T2). SubtreeSpecResolver(subject, childType, governingRoot, verb) -> Optional<Specification>: (1) inheritable-relation gate FIRST — childType must declare governingRoot.type inheritable (a plain childType->[ancestorType] Map, opt-in default-off), checked BEFORE any lookup so a non-inheritable list never hits the supplier; (2) resolve the role ONCE on the governing root (never per-ancestor — root-only, per-node is Phase 8); (3) verb gate verb in permissions[governingRoot.type]; grant -> Optional.of(subtreeOf(root)), else/any-exception -> Optional.empty(). CRITICAL correctness: the inheritable grant lives in permissions[ANCESTOR/root type], NOT permissions[child type] — mirrors category.rego inherited_grant (data.<t>.inheritable[child][ancestor] AND verb in role.permissions[ancestor.type]). This is what makes the widened LIST and a single-GET decide the SAME rows by construction. The inheritance Map is injected as a plain Map (not OpaAbacProperties) so opa-abac-spring-data keeps NO dependency on the starter (deps flow core<-spring-data<-starter).

name: Hierarchy-aware list composition: subtreeSpec OR-ed inside scope.and, notDenied AND-ed outside; batch carries ancestors
description: AbacQueryService 4-arg findAuthorized(repo, scope, ctx, subtreeSpec) for the hierarchy-aware list filter (5.5-B T3). Pure-SQL path: combined = scope.and( tagResidual.or(subtreeSpec) ).and( notDenied ). TWO load-bearing placements: (a) subtreeSpec OR-ed INSIDE scope.and(...) so the inheritable widening can NEVER escape the caller's catalogId scope (no cross-catalog leak); (b) notDenied AND-ed OUTSIDE the OR so a leaf deny overrides BOTH the tag branch AND the subtree branch (folding deny into the OR would re-admit denied rows). notDenied() = jsonb_extract_path_text(tags,'abac_deny') IS DISTINCT FROM 'true', expressed in Criteria as (value IS NULL) OR (value <> 'true') — absent tag -> kept (matches Rego not-denied on absent key), abac_deny=true -> excluded. The allowlist-BATCH path is independently hierarchy-aware: withResource resolves each candidate's ancestors and builds the 4-arg Resource(...,ancestors) so allowAll runs the SAME final_allow=(direct OR inherited) AND NOT denied as a single-GET; subtreeSpec is NOT applied on the batch path (redundant). The 3-arg findAuthorized stays byte-compatible (delegates with subtreeSpec=null); the new AncestorResolver ctor arg is NULLABLE (hierarchy off -> tag-only batch, fail-closed) so the always-on AbacQueryService bean wires whether or not a resolver bean exists (ObjectProvider). Fail-closed everywhere: failed subtree resolution -> narrower tag-only; batch per-row resolution failure -> empty ancestors -> direct-only; short/all-false allowAll drops rows; opa-abac-core untouched.

A multi-table ltree re-parent service (CatalogHierarchyService.reparentCategory) read the moving Category with the UNLOCKED categories.findById then mutated + @Version-bumped that same row (setParentId + saveAndFlush) before the native subtree path rewrite. This deviates from the repo's documented lock-first mutate posture (AbstractCrudService.mutate / getByIdForUpdate: 'lock the row FOR UPDATE so two concurrent mutations serialize and neither sees a stale @Version'). CategoryRepository already extends LockableJpaRepository so findByIdForUpdate was available and unused; the row write was only optimistically guarded (the native ltree UPDATE locks by path AFTER the entity mutate, not a JPA pessimistic read that refreshes the in-session @Version). Guides billed the re-parent as 'atomic', overselling an optimistic-only row guard.
resolution: Make the FIRST entity-touching read in a re-parent/mutate flow a pessimistic-locked read: categories.findByIdForUpdate(categoryId) instead of findById, so concurrent operations on the same row serialize at the SELECT ... FOR UPDATE lock. Rule of thumb: any @Transactional method whose first act is read-then-write of a row that other writers can touch should lead with the locked read (the documented mutate posture), not rely on optimistic @Version alone — especially when downstream native SQL (here the ltree subtree rewrite) makes a half-applied state visible to a racing reader.

description: Two @DataJpaTest ITs in the same package each declaring their own static @SpringBootApplication TestApp -> a THIRD one added in 5.5-B made @DataJpaTest's package auto-scan fail with 'Found multiple @SpringBootConfiguration annotated classes'. Surfaces ONLY when the full module suite runs (each IT passes in isolation), so a per-test run hides it — the ★ gate's full-suite run is what caught it. Also: a subtreeOf-based list IT came back empty because the test's LtreePathSource looked the ROOT's path up in the listed table (which holds only the child rows), but subtreeOf needs the ROOT's path and the root lives in another table.
resolution: Pin EVERY @DataJpaTest IT in a shared package to its own config via @ContextConfiguration(classes = <ThatIT>.TestApp.class) — this disables the ambiguous package scan. And: subtreeOf reads the ROOT's path from wherever the root lives; in a single-table test, the LtreePathSource must SYNTHESIZE a non-listed root's path from its label (e.g. catalog_<id>), mirroring the real per-table layout where each type has its own path column. Always run the FULL module suite at the ★ gate, never just the new test.

title: Slice 5.5-A (single-resource N-level hierarchical authorization) SHIPPED on feature/void3110/hierarchy-single-resource
rationale: Slice 5.5-A is implemented end-to-end across T1-T7 (branch feature/void3110/hierarchy-single-resource, not yet pushed): core ParentRef/abacParent/input.resource.ancestors (Spring-free, additive); the AncestorResolver SPI + ltree & recursive-CTE impls (fail-closed, throw-never-truncate); the opt-in AbstractHierarchicalEntity (ltree path + HierarchicalPathMaintainer with atomic single-table reparent AND cross-table reparentDescendantsInTable); the HierarchicalAuthorizer single-resource seam (direct OR (walk_ok AND inherited), role resolved ONCE on the governing root, fail-closed); the starter HierarchyAutoConfiguration (opt-in default-off, resolver chosen by property + @ConditionalOnBean(source)); the catalog example adoption (3 entities extend the hierarchical base, a Liquibase ltree migration with GiST indexes + recursive-CTE backfill, CategoryAuthorizer now uses the library walk, path-on-create wired); the Rego inherited_grant + deny-overrides clause in product.rego/category.rego gated by opt-in data.<pkg>.inheritable; and an e2e matrix (run-hierarchy-matrix.sh) proving inheritance + deny-overrides + a re-parent flip. Proven by: opa test 72/72 + an opa eval probe; ./gradlew build green (incl. example ddl-auto:validate boot); HierarchyAdoptionIT (real Postgres + the real ltree migration: insert-derives-path, resolver decodes the chain, cross-table re-parent flips the lineage). The live newman e2e run is deferred to the maintainer (Docker unreachable in the build env). Single-resource ONLY — the hierarchy-aware list filter (subtreeSpec composed with the Phase-5 residual) is the not-yet-built Slice 5.5-B; per-node independent grants are Phase 8 (ReBAC). Docs: docs/guides/HIERARCHICAL-AUTHORIZATION.md; package at docs/to-do/implemented/HIERARCHY-SINGLE-RESOURCE/.

name: Opt-in AbstractHierarchicalEntity + atomic ltree subtree re-parent (path maintenance off the entity)
description: Hierarchy is an OPT-IN persistent base AbstractHierarchicalEntity extends AbstractSecuredEntity, adding a denormalized ltree 'path' column (map String with @Column(columnDefinition=ltree) + @ColumnTransformer(write="?::ltree") so a bound String lands in the ltree column without an implicit cast) + abstract abacParent() + selfLabel(). Non-hierarchical secured entities keep extending AbstractSecuredEntity and pay nothing (no path column). A leaf's missing parent FK (e.g. Product has no catalogId) is solved by the path encoding the full lineage, not a redundant column. Path MAINTENANCE lives OFF the entity in a HierarchicalPathMaintainer service (a @MappedSuperclass can't run native SQL; keeping it in a service mirrors AbstractCrudService.mutate write-centralization and makes re-parent one transactional unit): assignPath derives path=parent.path||self-label, throwing on a declared-but-missing parent path (broken lineage, fail-closed); reparent rewrites the ENTIRE moved subtree ATOMICALLY in ONE ltree UPDATE 'SET path = CASE WHEN nlevel(path)=oldDepth THEN newSelfPath ELSE newSelfPath || subpath(path, oldDepth) END WHERE path <@ oldSelfPath' — the CASE is REQUIRED because subpath(path, nlevel(path)) is an invalid ltree position for the moved node's own row. A re-parent under one's own descendant is rejected up-front (cycle guard). Atomicity is a single-statement DB guarantee: a UNIQUE(path) collision mid-rewrite rolls the whole UPDATE back (tree unchanged) — proven by a Testcontainers IT using TransactionTemplate for COMMITTED units of work (not @DataJpaTest rollback) so the re-parent and its rollback are observable across transactions. Only the table identifier is interpolated (regex-validated); all values are bound params.

title: Base-entity layer: opa-abac-spring-data, plain UUID ids, tags on the secure base, mutate() as the safe write default
rationale: Foundational domain-model design for the clean-room starter (the DOMAIN-MODEL-FOUNDATION slice). Decisions: (1) the reusable base stack (AbstractAuditableEntity, AbstractSecuredEntity, ResourceTags + converter, LockableJpaRepository, AbstractCrudService) lives in opa-abac-spring-data — it already depends on opa-abac-core + spring-boot-starter-data-jpa, and opa-abac-core MUST stay Spring-free, so JPA/Spring annotations cannot live in core. (2) Trim typed-id value objects: use a plain UUID id. Our ABAC layer (AbacContext, AbacDataObject) is String/UUID-based and no planned feature consumes a typed id, so a wrapper is pure ceremony; reintroducible additively later. (3) Tags live ONLY on the SECURE base (AbstractSecuredEntity), never the plain one, and the secure base implements AbacDataObject so a secured entity is authorizable out of the box (the fix for 'secure = just a marker'). (4) JSONB tags via @JdbcTypeCode(SqlTypes.JSON) + an AttributeConverter (idiomatic on Hibernate 6.4) rather than a hand-rolled UserType. (5) Timestamps are OffsetDateTime + @TimeZoneStorage(NATIVE) -> timestamptz, matching the existing CatalogEntity.createdAt. (6) Concurrency: expose getById (unlocked) AND getByIdForUpdate (pessimistic) explicitly, and make mutate(id, fn) (lock+mutate+save) the safe-by-default write path — the generalized fix for inconsistent locking discipline that causes stale-@Version lost-update races. Verify serialization with a latch-forced concurrency IT on real Postgres (not H2). @AutoTag auto-tagging is deferred (tags set explicitly for now).

description: Pre-implementation audit of shipped code before Phase-5 (data filtering) surfaced two reconciliation gotchas the plan didn't anticipate: (a) ./gradlew build goes RED the moment OpaClient gains abstract methods, because two test beans implement it as lambdas; (b) a naively-derived partial-eval 'filter' rule would inherit the shipped 'allow' rule's subject-roles fallback and return the WHOLE TABLE for a request with no role definition — a fail-OPEN list leak.
resolution: Both baked into the DATA-FILTERING plan. (1) BUILD-BREAKER: OpaClient is currently a single-method functional interface; two test beans implement it as LAMBDAS (PermissiveSecurityTestConfig.allowAllOpaClient in catalog, AbacTestConfig.inProcessTeamOpaClient in user-service) plus a named StubOpaClient in the starter test. Adding ADR-0005 abstract compile()+allowAll() makes OpaClient NON-functional, so both lambdas fail to compile; convert all three test impls to named/anonymous classes (compile->denyAll, allowAll->all-false as stubs) in the same commit as the interface change. 'Additive to the library contract' != 'zero-touch for tests'. (2) FAIL-OPEN LIST LEAK: shipped category/catalog/product.rego 'allow' has a subject-roles fallback (not has_role_definition -> grant read from JWT roles). The Phase-5 'filter' rule must be ROLE-DEFINITION-ONLY (model on team.rego, which dropped the fallback) so a missing role def -> DENY_ALL -> empty list. (3) Residual Specification must be AND-ed with the existing path scoping (findByCatalogId/findByCategoryId), never replace it; resolve role on the governing parent like CategoryAuthorizer. (4) Sequencing: Phase 5 ships BEFORE Phase 6.5, so 'filter' stays FLAT-VERB (category:read) — category expansion (ADR 0007) is a later additive retrofit; don't anticipate it. (5) allowAll is a SHARED primitive (Phase-6 enrichment consumes it) — design it general-public. All baked into DATA-FILTERING/{00-DESIGN,01-DECOMPOSITION,AUTONOMOUS-IMPLEMENTATION-PROMPT,10-QA-TEST-CASES} + cross-referenced to ADRs 0005/0006/0007.

description: Multi-type roles (permissions on >1 resource type) made OPA /v1/compile emit a DNF disjunct per granted type, each guarded by eq(<type>, input.resource.type); CompileResponseParser poisoned the whole residual on the first foreign-type binding, so EVERY realistic multi-type role silently degraded lists from the pure-SQL residual path to the allowlist-batch fallback (decision-identical with the fallback on — invisible to every row-set test; over-deny with it off). The filter matrix's own readers+curator all ran the batch path. Found only by reading the Postgres statement log during a doc-capture session.
resolution: Fold, don't poison: a disjunct guarded by eq on a DIFFERENT definite STRING type is identically false for this table's rows -> DROP it (narrowing-safe); contradiction wins over unsupported siblings in the same conjunction. CRITICAL SUBTLETY (caught by adversarial review, empirically via opa eval --partial): all-disjuncts-folded must map to unsupported()/batch-recheck, NOT clean DENY_ALL — an all-foreign filter residual cannot speak for policy-side inheritance (subtreeSpec widening is DECLINED for tag-gated/denial-carrying roles on the assumption the batch covers them), and a clean deny would empty lists whose rows single-GET allows. Mechanism-level pins: parser MT tests on the real wire shape + consumer never-batches verify; row-set e2e cannot distinguish the two paths.
